correction: Added a mathematically checked explanatory TikZ schematic of two refined wall segments shared by one left cell and two right cells.

diagram_math_checks.evidence: The left cell has cyclic boundary a=(0,0), q=(0,1.5), b=(0,3), l1=(-3,3.4), l0=(-3,-0.5), with q collinear on its right wall. The right cells are triangles (a,r0,q) and (q,r1,b), where r0=(3,0.5), r1=(3,2.6). They are convex and intersect the left cell in exactly [a,q] and [q,b], respectively; the right cells intersect only at q. This is the refined-cell interface of proof step 3.1.

q is the common endpoint of the two right cells, so the left cell is explicitly subdivided there. The outer lower segments l0-a-r0 are collinear and the upper segments l1-b-r1 are collinear (both cross products computed as zero); a and b can therefore be wall-intersection subdivision points rather than additional original vertices sharing the projection of q. The picture is explicitly local, not an entire polygon or a choice of all its original vertices.

diagram_math_checks.check: Interior points and nondegenerate fan triangles
diagram_math_checks.evidence: For pL=(-1.5,1.45), p-=(1,0.65), p+=(1,2.37), computed oriented fan triangle areas in cyclic boundary order are respectively [1.125,1.125,2.625,2.925,2.55], [0.725,0.775,0.75], and [0.755,0.745,0.75]. All are positive, sum to the cell areas 10.35, 2.25, 2.25, and verify the points are interior and all eleven fan triangles nondegenerate, as required in step 4.1.

The left fan uses both [a,q] and [q,b]. The lower and upper right fans use precisely those respective segments, so adjacent triangles meet in full refined edges; all other intersections are shared radial edges, endpoints, or empty. The compiled standalone view shows all eleven triangles and the whole left and right boundaries; explicit named-node closing segments are present, with no --cycle. This agrees with L1 and the supplier definition, which permits subdivision and interior vertices.
Original Statement, Facts, and every proof step are byte-preserved. The figure occurs only in final Remarks and the explanation explicitly says the proof is independent of it.
